_comment: Outbound write channels — everywhere this app would send something to a real person or system.
Copy to config/channels.json and edit; that file is gitignored.
Reads and writes are kept apart deliberately. config/connectors.json is what we may look at;
this file is what we may say. A misconfigured read returns nothing; a misconfigured write posts
in the company's name to a stranger, and cannot be taken back.
status  'implemented' — the code path exists and runs when its credentials are present.
'planned'     — deliberately not built. The notes say what it would actually take,
because every one of these is its own separate problem and pretending
otherwise is how you ship a button that silently does nothing.
Nothing is ever sent without an explicit submit/send on the request. Drafting is free and
reversible; sending is neither, and the two stay separate calls.

_notes: A fine-grained personal access token with Issues: read and write on this repo is enough.
The issue is the audit record: it opens with the public complaint and the reporters' own
words, and every later step in the loop — reporter contacted, fix landed, reporter
confirmed — is appended as a comment on it. Read top to bottom it is the whole history of
one complaint, which is the point.

outbound.label: GitHub issues
outbound.notes: Files the ticket and appends every subsequent loop step to it as a comment.

outbound.label: Email
outbound.notes: Needs a sending domain with SPF/DKIM set up and a Mailgun (or equivalent) account in front of it. Sending cold mail from a fresh domain mostly lands in spam, so this is a deliverability project before it is a code project.

outbound.label: Reddit
outbound.notes: Credentials already exist in .env. The work is the OAuth script-app flow plus the fact that a new account replying about a product reads as astroturfing and gets shadowbanned — needs an account with history and per-subreddit self-promotion rules respected.

outbound.label: Hacker News
outbound.notes: No write API — replies go through a logged-in session and a form post. Easier than the others mechanically. HN is unusually hostile to corporate voice, so the reply has to read as a person.

outbound.label: X
outbound.notes: Posting needs OAuth 2.0 user context, not the app-only bearer token used for reading, and a paid tier for write access.
